searchText: <@552133098075193354> I believe you are referring to selfish mining attacks which increase in profitability the larger the ratio of fees to block reward. There is an academic paper about it, and it has been talked about/referenced a lot in the past but I'm not sure if there is a nice "consumer friendly" version anywhere. 1559 solves it by simply reducing transaction fees to near 0 so that ratio remains *very* low. MEV goes beyond only selfish mining, where i interpret selfish mining as mining on your private chain and releasing strategically to orphan other blocks time bandit attacks for instance, where a miner does a short reorg to capture a high fee-paying transaction. this is somewhat mitigated by 1559 since basefee is burnt, but you can have high tips when there are bots trying to frontrun in a bidding war then there is MEV where the miner simply censors such transactions that attempt to arbitrage some situation, and the miner includes its own transaction instead to capture the arbitrage. 1559 doesn't change anything in this case is the academic paper you mention "on the instability of bitcoin without the block reward"? Correct <@486501030046203915>. That sounds like the paper I'm thinking of, been a while since I have looked it up though. I just remember it from a picture it has on the first page or two. 😬 yes it discusses selfish mining. the original paper by gun sirer et al. focused more on selfish mining to capture the block reward, but that one shows it's even profitable in a regime where transaction fees dominate The one I am thinking of specifically talks about a profitable selfish mining strategy in a system where transaction fees dominate. Must be the one you mentioned. So, again, not an expert as all, but AIUI, there is _also_ a concern about re-orgs when txn fees get quite large. If, for example, the txn fee is 10x the block reward, doesn't it make sense to re-org up to 10 blocks to make sure you captured those txn fees vs. another miner? Are you thinking of the selfish mining attack we were discussing above? Selfish mining attacks can incentdvize every miner essentially to mine their own chain in the most pathological case. Ah yeah, sorry, still having my first coffee 😅 I believe it's closer to the time bandit attack <@!486501030046203915> mentioned. I think you might be referring to this: https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~arvindn/publications/mining_CCS.pdf
